## Solution

**Yes**, such a line bundle exists.

**Proof.** Let $X$ be a smooth projective curve of genus $g \geq 2$ over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $K_X$ denote the canonical bundle, with $\deg K_X = 2g-2$.

**Step 1: Compute $h^0(L)$ for any line bundle of degree $2g-1$.**

Let $L$ be a line bundle with $\deg L = 2g-1$. By Riemann–Roch:
$$h^0(L) - h^1(L) = \deg L - g + 1 = (2g-1) - g + 1 = g.$$
By Serre duality, $h^1(L) = h^0(K_X \otimes L^{-1})$. Since
$$\deg(K_X \otimes L^{-1}) = (2g-2) - (2g-1) = -1 < 0,$$
and a line bundle of negative degree admits no nonzero global sections, we have $h^1(L) = 0$. Therefore:
$$h^0(L) = g \quad \text{for every } L \in \operatorname{Pic}^{2g-1}(X).$$

**Step 2: Characterize when $L$ fails to be globally generated.**

The line bundle $L$ is generated by global sections if and only if for every point $p \in X$, the evaluation map $H^0(X,L) \to L|_p \cong \mathbb{C}$ is surjective, equivalently $h^0(L(-p)) = h^0(L) - 1$.

Fix $p \in X$ and apply Riemann–Roch to $L(-p)$, which has degree $2g-2$:
$$h^0(L(-p)) - h^1(L(-p)) = (2g-2) - g + 1 = g - 1.$$
By Serre duality, $h^1(L(-p)) = h^0(K_X \otimes L^{-1}(p))$, and
$$\deg(K_X \otimes L^{-1}(p)) = (2g-2) - (2g-1) + 1 = 0.$$
A degree-zero line bundle has $h^0 = 1$ if it is trivial and $h^0 = 0$ otherwise. Hence:
$$h^0(L(-p)) = g - 1 + h^0(K_X \otimes L^{-1}(p)) = \begin{cases} g & \text{if } K_X \otimes L^{-1}(p) \cong \mathcal{O}_X, \\ g-1 & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases}$$

So $L$ fails to be globally generated at $p$ (i.e., every section vanishes at $p$) if and only if $h^0(L(-p)) = h^0(L) = g$, which happens if and only if:
$$L \cong K_X(p).$$

Therefore:
$$L \text{ is **not** globally generated} \iff \exists\, p \in X \text{ such that } L \cong K_X(p).$$

**Step 3: Show the "bad" locus is a proper subvariety, so a good $L$ exists.**

Consider the map
$$\varphi: X \longrightarrow \operatorname{Pic}^{2g-1}(X), \quad p \mapsto K_X(p).$$
This map is injective: if $K_X(p) \cong K_X(q)$, then $\mathcal{O}_X(p) \cong \mathcal{O}_X(q)$, which for a curve of genus $g \geq 1$ forces $p = q$ (otherwise $X$ would admit a degree-one map to $\mathbb{P}^1$, implying $g = 0$). Thus the image $\varphi(X)$ is a **1-dimensional** (closed) subvariety of $\operatorname{Pic}^{2g-1}(X)$.

The Picard variety $\operatorname{Pic}^{2g-1}(X)$ has dimension $g$. Since $g \geq 2$, we have $\dim \varphi(X) = 1 < g = \dim \operatorname{Pic}^{2g-1}(X)$, so $\varphi(X)$ is a **proper** closed subset.

Consequently, there exist line bundles $L \in \operatorname{Pic}^{2g-1}(X) \setminus \varphi(X)$. For any such $L$, there is no point $p$ with $L \cong K_X(p)$, so by Step 2, $L$ is generated by global sections.

**Conclusion.** For every smooth projective curve $X$ of genus $g \geq 2$ over $\mathbb{C}$, there exists a line bundle $L$ of degree $2g-1$ that is generated by global sections. In fact, the globally generated line bundles form a dense open subset of $\operatorname{Pic}^{2g-1}(X)$, with complement being the 1-dimensional subvariety $\{K_X(p) : p \in X\}$. $\blacksquare$
